evidenceBoundary: Deterministic local-process tests on this host only. No cloud inference, production deployment, or external command was invoked.
problemRecovered: Persistent interactive TerminalSession.kill() called only the PTY root kill operation, whereas bounded command execution already used platform process-tree termination. A terminal-root descendant therefore had a weaker cancellation guarantee.

change.interactiveLifecycle: TerminalSession.kill() now invokes the shared terminateProcessTreeByPid implementation used by bounded execution.
change.platformBehavior: Windows uses taskkill /T /F with a direct-child fallback; POSIX attempts the process group before the root fallback.

combinedRegression.command: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/terminal/test/terminal.test.ts packages/server/test/runtime.test.ts packages/server/test/run-failure.test.ts packages/tools/test/command-exit-status.test.ts

proven: A real supported PTY session whose root starts a child process terminates without that child later writing its orphan marker.
Timeout, abort, process-tree cleanup, workspace removal, output streaming, and command-service terminal completion remain covered by the adjacent regressions.
Command nonzero exits remain structured failures rather than successful observations.
notProven: Every Windows desktop, shell, antivirus, or process-permission configuration.
Absence of console flashes in a freshly rebuilt packaged Electron application.
Long-lived interactive user-terminal behavior under arbitrary child-process trees.
requiredNextEvidence: Build a fresh isolated desktop artifact and run a visible Windows smoke test covering persistent terminal launch, nested npm/cmd child cancellation, output streaming, no console flash, and immediate workspace cleanup.
